title: Counter-Liberation: How People Without a Culture Might Get One Back
author: Kim C. Domenico
content:
![](https://www.counterpunch.org/wp-
content/uploads/2026/08/Screenshot-2026-08-06-at-3.49.31-PM-680x486.png)

Photo by [Andreas
M](https://unsplash.com/@nextvoyage_pl?utm_source=unsplash&utm_medium=referral&utm_content=creditCopyText)

> …the next great division of the world will be between people who wish to
> live as creatures and people who wish to live as machines.

> –Wendell Berry,  _Life Is A Miracle_
>
> The old world is running up like “parchment in the fire,” and nobody who
> wants to be part of the new one can be seen to defend it.
>
> –Paul Kingsnorth,  _Against the Machine_
>
> The culture has been damaged…by an idiotic distrust of all ideas, religions
> and literature handed down to us by elders and ancestors.
>
> –Robert Bly,  _The Sibling Society_

> The right kind of warrior takes on his own internal demons before he sails
> out to take on those of others….most of all, he works to clear out his own
> inner junkyard so that he can go searching for truth—and recognize it when
> he finds it….what he is fighting for is the love he so often fails at. His
> most effective weapon is sacrifice.
>
> – Kingsnorth,  _Ibid_.

Among my female social acquaintances in the “aging” category, where I too
reside, it seems many of us are caring for a disabled husband. My friend
Rachel reports to me that another friend, Maria, more acquaintance than close
friend, whom she ran into at a social gathering last week, unexpectedly
blurted out her exasperation: “I did not sign up for this!”

Of course, this is exactly what she _did_ sign up for. But, wedding vows being
one of those things that is “ _part of what we used to be and are no longer,_
” she, not being a trad-wife, suffers those feelings of deep frustration as
she hangs in, alone, unthanked, way less picturesquely than a back-to-the-
lander churning butter or heating with wood fire, sacrificing, and _for what?_
For many years I have pondered the seeming incommensurability of such
traditions of staying, of rootedness in a culture, with that  _something else_
that tells us we're free  _not to_. In truth, this certainty, that one ought
not have to put up with absurdly confining circumstances comes as if
naturally; it makes defending old ways something a liberal does not do. That
something else, so difficult to limn, I've long called liberal reality. But
I'm still working on what liberalism  _does_ that makes cultural rootedness
something that  _used to be_ , something our ancestors had, that indigenous
people have, but we do not.

This lack wouldn't be so bad if I were happy without it, but I'm not. So, this
is what happens when a white middle-class educated person takes her
unhappiness seriously – that something really  _is_ wrong, and it might not be
her! It might be what was given to her without her asking, the culture
substitute, the non-sugar sweetener for the brutalization that cultural
erasure is. I will still call it by its blander name, liberalism, but
liberalism is the smooth-talking agent of the Machine.

Paul Kingsnorth's book,  _Against the Machine_ , has provided me with much
help with the discernment of this darkening of civilization. Like Kingsnorth,
since childhood I've had the persistent feeling that “something always felt
bent out of shape. As if there was some hidden wound beneath it all.” All my
writings have been to shape ideas that could help me remove the blame from
myself for this wrongness, my servile ego telling me  _the problem is you_.
These ideas of returning to the limiting circumstances that make culture, and
therefore humanity – not to mention a future for creatures, not machines -
possible, are non-romantic. I know that in my writing about this return to
living within limitations, I use the word “suffering” frequently. It is not
bliss. Maybe the better goal is the one Freud suggested for mental health:
“ordinary unhappiness.” For in achieving liberation from neuroses, one is
freed sufficiently to “work and to love,” no small freedom!

That the “internal demons must be taken on first” is another point upon which
Kingsnorth and I agree. However, as one who enthusiastically absorbed
mythologist Joseph Campbell's adage to “Follow your bliss,” and who has
promoted the path of the artist as the way of defiance of the Machine open to
all, I really do want it both ways! Though Campbell is seen by some Christian
critics as advocating bliss-without-pain, that is a one-sided view. To the
contrary, in encouraging people to take on the risky mythic journey of one's
own life's “adventure,” Campbell was, exactly, pointing to the way of
sacrifice that leads to revivifying a moribund culture. That is, 'bliss' may
not be a strictly personal goal. Admittedly, even though “sacrifice” was a
major part of his message, Campbell tended to minimize the role of suffering.
But he knew, as I do, mythic truth is the creative outcome of human
embodiment. Myth's imaginative meaning is derived from biological
“determinism” and its realm of suffering that's now optional.

Thanks to modern-day transpersonal psychological practices derived from the
Freudian heritage, I have experienced the “mythic journey,” (a journey that
does not have an endpoint before death). Since then, I've believed my lifeway
choices should be in obedience to the truth of the completely interdependent
reality that journey had connected me with. In my soul I knew endless growth
(progress) is incompatible with spiritual reality.  _God 's truth, that is, is
one that comes with limits. _

The “downscale,” traditional choices Orin and I made previously which I have
listed many times and do not wish to bore readers with again, admirable in the
eyes of some, coalesced in the creation of our popular, beloved Cafe in Uptown
Utica - in its public representation of the metaphysical reality of “all-
connected.. That is, we began our small business with blissful enthusiasm,
trusting that (enough) “money would follow,” but fully aware of the terrifying
risk we took in leaping without a safety net. For 22 years, the Cafe, in its
full-hearted affirmation of the purely human, provided us with what felt like
a cultural base.

+++

One more important contributor to the “downscale,” self-limiting lifeway
choices that prepared the way for the Cafe, though implied in the taking on of
the Campbellian mythic journey, must be explicitly mentioned. It is that
taking on of “internal demons.”(see epigraph) The choices Orin and I made to
self-limit came from two souls that had been deeply wounded. That did not make
the choices, thogh coming from alienation,  _bad_ or _questionable._ Limiting
as they were, stranding us socially as outsiders, our opinions on practically
every item on the liberal agenda not agreeing with our liberal friends, the
choices weren't wrong, only  _impossible to defend inside liberal reality._
Underlying trauma gave us the key to finding a perspective that could approve
our illiberal choices. That is, because trauma wounds to the soul are and must
be denied in liberal reality, they serve as  _the inward colonizer._ Trauma is
the all-powerful driver of the severe limitation on the larger self that
everyone in liberal reality is subject to, known as neurosis. Thus trauma, as
it turns out, offers not only __ the potential for living life within
limitations _,_ but the very evidence that the limiting framework is humanly
necessary _._ Trauma-made-conscious makes it possible for uncomfortable
alienation __ to be understood as  _inside_ of a larger truer reality, beyond
liberalism.

That is, few of us white liberals, given our conditioning, are prepared for
the particular distress of taking upon oneself lifestyle limitations. To some
of these limitations a level of admiration still accrues ( i.e., limited use
of digital technology, subsistence farming, staying in the inner city
neighborhood and schools). Others are the kind that are just no longer
necessary, that have been roundly renounced as outmoded freedom restrictions,
and no longer trouble anyone any more, such as commitments to home, family and
place as duties of the heart. The connection between the two kinds of moral
decision-making – socially/environmentally conscious (admirable) and
rootedness in place and family (unnecessarily restrictive, value-relative) -
is no longer seen. Most who defend the old ways - Catholics or other kinds of
conservatives or traditionalists - have their beliefs to fall back on. For
liberals, however, the cry- let's call it agonized, for it could be - “I never
signed on for this!” - is sign of _crisis,_ the consequence of the fact that
limitations of traditional roles and obligations go against the entire liberal
liberationist meaning.__ For liberals _,_ there's no metaphysical foundation
to fall back on, no way to confirm meaning in this kind of completely
“optional” suffering, no way, anymore, of reasonably accepting that there's no
solution.

Of course, the larger free-market meaning of liberalism is our true shared
foundation of meaning, whether liberal or conservative (in money we trust).
But the confirmed liberal, having abandoned traditional belief, theoretically
open to “reason,” possibly attracted to Campbell's follow your bliss message
but not to its inward, downward dimension - is _in a spiritually desperate
position whether she knows it or not._ That is, her unhappiness – as long as
addictions/distractions do not become a detour, as they do for most – is the
means to find meaning precisely in the apparent meaningless suffering of the
limitations liberalism has made obsolete. For this reason, in liberalism, both
the reality of trauma and of imagination-based, metaphysical truth are denied.
This is no accident!

+++

The crisis one experiences in facing the excruciating unacceptability of
limitation is legitimate. I do not know the details of Maria's frustration,
but having lived for several years now with Orin's severe PTSD, I can readily
imagine her details are real! Not one thing in our training in liberal reality
prepares us - despite the words of the wedding vows about loving and
cherishing - for the  _for worse._ Without a story that could give one a
single reason to stick, to settle, to stay, rather than to escape,  _what
then?_

Crucially, it must be seen that the person expressing those spirited and
sympathy-inspiring words, “I did not sign up for this,”  _is_ also  _coming
from untreated trauma._ That is, no one existing in modern secular reality, in
the absence of a sacred order, can escape trauma wounds. Women, who tend to
live longer, must more often have the frustration of the spouse's infirmity,
but  _the wall of desperation_ they run up against is of liberal making!
_Not_ because the truth is they must bend to God's will – not exactly, anyway.
I have no silver bullet to offer that removes suffering (though I'm not fool
enough to deny money helps!). However, this imprisoning wall is built upon the
false liberal gospel of freedom _._ That is, in a certain way, despite liberal
progressive expectations - suffering  _is_ our lot. But it comes with its
“antidote.” For those who will feel their  _authentic, unresolvable_ pain,
bringing it out from under denial, the gift of imagination is again possible.
Imagination is the way, God-given, of transforming/transcending the suffering
of life lived humanly, within natural limitations. As Freud knew, neuroses and
creativity spring from the same soil (the soul).

This is not to say don't give yourself the relief of in-home care for the
disabled husband if you can afford it. Nor is it to say one must stick when
there is threat of physical or mental harm. But in a way, what I'm saying is
it's better when what you face can be seen as having  _no solution_. No
escape. Liberal faith is embedded in airiness as well as in misplaced trust in
technology, faith in a solution that will, in turn, allow one to escape this
intolerable reality  _I didn 't sign up for_. When you think about it, what
better way could there be for a liberal to learn that being right is not
always right? Aren't we now being faced with realizing that the conviction
(i.e., that Trump is evil) doesn't help with the reality of the destructive
trajectory of globalization? If there is help, being right isn't it. Knowing –
and resenting - what is wrong with the other _isn 't it_.

+++

The ways of avoiding finality are countless. Even parenthood has its available
– and non-controversial - loopholes, from reversible vasectomies to  _in_
_vitro_ fertilization, from formula milk to babysitting by screen. Our good-
byes, nowadays, can always be penultimate. There is not one thing about
opposition to the Machine - that is, to defending our humanity - that is easy
or simple, any more than uprooting and moving out to the Midwest plains in
1850 was simple or easy. It's counter-intuitive, counter-reasonable, counter-
liberation! It is that process of settling the West, but now in reverse. It is
staying. We adapt in a thousand ways to the given Machine reality, in part
because to do otherwise is so effortful, so weird, so lonely, so completely
unnecessary from the everyday point of view, but also because its goods are so
unequivocally, unarguably  _good._ They make us happy, or as happy as we can
be in a context of dissolving social bonds. Refuse to adapt, in a condition in
which we are already fully assimilated? This is the incredible, perhaps
insurmountable challenge of refusing Machinehood.

Thus it is not possible or feasible to spend my breath trying to convince
people to do what I do! My anti-liberation slant cannot possibly be extolled
or made inspiring to others. I don't even know what  _I 'm_ doing, so how
could I persuade others! But, still, inspired by Kingsnorth's warrior spirit
(and the others whose shoulders he stands on), I can help to delineate the
Machine so that others, who want more than anything to  _see,_ to understand
what is happening in this reality which we cannot see or touch, but can feel.
Perhaps those of us, “woke” but still blind in liberal reality, can begin to
grasp what is happening to us, why everything is getting worse, something
sensed but for which we as yet lack words. We try to name what we ardently
oppose – patriarchy, hierarchy, capitalism, globalism, neoliberalism, fascism,
Trumpism etc., but the words do not quite hit the mark.

Many poets, prophets and committed religious visionaries have hit this mark.
The problem is metaphysical, not purely political, economic, or social, not
even purely “spiritual.” People who have freed themselves from religion, from
a sacred order, cannot have a clue except insofar as they relinquish their
power to deny the disorder in their souls, the tendency to neurosis and self-
preoccupation, infinitely deniable in liberal reality, and except they take
the longing in their hearts as the direction to follow, leading back to a
culture and the commitments that make a culture, whether or not we arrive
there.
